questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Somalia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Daraawiish State” part of the Somalia article.

questions.proof: This became Italian Somalia in 1905, with capital Mogadishu.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Somalia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Somalia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Somalia article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Djibouti to the northwest, Kenya to the southwest, with Yemen to the north, the Guardafui Channel and Somali Sea to the east, and Ethiopia to the west.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Shortly afterwards, World War 2 broke out and he invaded British Somaliland, but two years later the British returned and liberated British Somaliland and _____ as well as taking over Italian Somaliland.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Somaliland”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “World War 2 history” part of the Somalia article.

questions.proof: Shortly afterwards, World War 2 broke out and he invaded British Somaliland, but two years later the British returned and liberated British Somaliland and Ethiopia as well as taking over Italian Somaliland.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “_____ offered to buy the rights to the east Africa coast from Oman, who was in charge of protecting the cities and small kingdoms there, and Oman agreed.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “offered”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Somalia article, under the heading “Daraawiish State”.

questions.proof: Italy offered to buy the rights to the east Africa coast from Oman, who was in charge of protecting the cities and small kingdoms there, and Oman agreed.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In ancient times, Somalia was a place where people from _____ and Arabia went to buy gum arabic, myrrh and ebony wood.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “people”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Somalia article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In ancient times, Somalia was a place where people from Egypt and Arabia went to buy gum arabic, myrrh and ebony wood.
